Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Fussilat (Fussilat, "Explained in Detail"), because it opens with the verse that points to the Qur'an's verses being made distinct, namely His saying, ﴿A Book whose verses have been detailed﴾. It is thereby distinguished from the other surahs of the Ha Meem group (al-Hawamim).

On the Objectives of the Surah

• Extolling the Qur'an and its guidance, and affirming its truthfulness and its protection from falsehood reaching it; establishing the reality of the Messenger (ﷺ), that he is a human being to whom Allah revealed, so that he would be a guide and a caller to His true religion; and warning those who deny the verses of the Qur'an.

• Discussion of the creation of the heavens and the earth; rebuking and reproaching the polytheists for their disbelief in the Creator of the heavens and the earth, along with the evidences in their creation of His sole divinity; reminding them of the fate of the deniers before them; warning them of the punishment of the Hereafter; and cautioning them against the companions from among the jinn and mankind who adorn disbelief for them; and contrasting all of that with the honour that the monotheists have with Allah.

• Strengthening the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers with Allah's support for them; directing the believer to repel evil with what is better, to be patient over the harshness of the hostile, and to ward off evil by seeking refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

• Mention of the proofs of Allah's sole creation of great creatures such as the sun and the moon, and of the signs He placed in the horizons and in the selves, and the proofs of the possibility of resurrection; and a warning to those who deviate regarding these manifest signs, or turn a blind eye to them, and so disbelieve in them.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.
This noble Qur'an is a revelation from the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, which He sent down upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).
This is a Book whose verses have been made fully clear, and whose meanings and rulings have been explained. It is an Arabic Qur'an, easy to understand for a people who know the Arabic language.

Bringing good news of reward, both in this world and the next, to those who believe in it and act upon its guidance, and giving warning of punishment, both in this world and the next, to those who disbelieve in it. Yet most people turn away from it, for they do not listen to it with the listening of acceptance and response.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 5:

So act according to your religion, just as we are acting according to our religion."

Say, [O Messenger], to them: "I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God, the one who deserves worship, is one God, with no partner. So they have no sincerity toward the Creator and no benefit to offer creation. And they do not believe in the Resurrection, nor in Paradise and Hellfire.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 8:

Indeed, those who believed in Allah, His Messenger, and His Book, and did righteous deeds, sincerely devoted to Allah in them, will have a great reward that is neither cut off nor withheld.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists, rebuking them and expressing astonishment at their deed: "Do you indeed disbelieve in Allah, who created the earth in two days, and set up for Him equals and partners whom you worship besides Him? That Creator is the Lord of all the worlds."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 10:

He, glorified is He, placed in the earth firm mountains above it, and blessed it, making it constantly bountiful for its inhabitants. He determined in it the provisions of its inhabitants, in food and whatever sustains them of livelihood, all within four complete days: two days in which He created the earth, and two days in which He placed in it firm mountains and determined in it its sustenance, "equally for those who ask," meaning: for whoever wishes to inquire about that, so that he may know it.

Then He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, turned (istawa) to the heaven, meaning He intended toward the heaven, and it was smoke before that. He said to the heaven and to the earth: "Submit to My command, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We have come in submission to You; we have no will that opposes Your will."

Then Allah decreed the creation of the seven heavens and their perfecting in two days, and thus the creation of the heavens and the earth was completed in six days, for a wisdom known to Allah, although He is able, glorified be He, to create them in a single moment. He revealed in each heaven what He willed and what He commanded in it. We adorned the lowest heaven with shining stars, and as a protection for it from the devils who eavesdrop. That wondrous creation is the decree of the Almighty in His dominion, the All-Knowing whose knowledge encompasses everything.

If they turn away after all this, these deniers, after the praiseworthy qualities of the Qur'an and the attributes of the Mighty God have been made clear to them, then say to them: "I have warned you of a punishment that will uproot you, like the punishment of 'Ad and Thamud when they disbelieved in their Lord and disobeyed His messengers."

When the messengers came to them, one after another, to 'Ad and Thamud, urging them to worship Allah alone with no partner, they said to their messengers: "If our Lord had willed to send down to us angels as messengers, He would have sent down angels from the heavens with what you call us to. He did not send you, who are mere humans like us. Indeed, we deny that with which Allah has sent you to us, of belief in Allah alone."

As for ʿĀd, the people of Hūd, they exalted themselves in the land over the servants of God without any right. They said, in their delusion, "Who is stronger than us?" Did they not see that God, who created them, is stronger than them in power and in might? And they used to deny Our signs and proofs.

So We sent upon them a wind, extremely cold and loud, on days of ill omen for them, that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace and humiliation in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is even more humiliating, and they will not be helped, by having the punishment averted from them.

As for Thamud, the people of Salih, We had made clear to them the path of truth and the way of right guidance, but they chose blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them, because of the sins they committed through their disbelief in Allah and their denial of His messengers.
We saved those who believed from the punishment that seized ʿĀd and Thamūd, and those who were saved were fearing Allah and guarding themselves against Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 24:

Whether they endure patiently or not, the Fire is their abode. And if they ask to be returned to the world so that they may resume righteous deeds, they will not be granted that, and their excuses will not be accepted.

We have appointed for these wrongdoers who deny [the truth] companions who made fair-seeming to them what lay before them and what lay behind them [of worldly matters and of the Hereafter]... 

Wait, I need to translate the passage as given, not the verse alone. Here is the translation:

We appointed for these wrongdoers, who deny [the truth], corrupt companions from among the devils of mankind and jinn. They made appealing to them the ugly deeds they committed in this world, and they urged them toward its pleasures and its forbidden desires. They also made appealing to them what lay behind them of matters of the Hereafter, so they caused them to forget its remembrance, and they urged them to deny the Resurrection. Thereby they deserved to enter the Fire along with previous communities of disbelieving jinn and humans. Indeed, they were losers: they lost their deeds in this world, and themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.

The disbelievers say to one another, urging each other on: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and do not obey it or submit to its commands. Raise your voices with shouting, whistling, and noise against Muhammad (ﷺ) when he recites the Qur'an, so that perhaps you will overpower him, and he will stop reciting, and we will prevail over him."

Then We will surely make those who said this statement taste a severe punishment in this world and in the Hereafter, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of the evil deeds they used to do.

That severe punishment is a just recompense for the enemies of Allah: it is the Fire of Hell, in which they will have the abode of everlasting eternity. It is a recompense for their denying Our signs and proofs in the worldly life. The verse indicates the great gravity of the crime of one who turns people away from the Great Qur'an and bars them from contemplating it and being guided by it, by whatever means.

﴿And those who disbelieved will say, while they are in the Fire: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn and mankind, and we will place them beneath our feet so that they will be among the lowest of the Fire."﴾

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 30:

Indeed, those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," alone, with no partner, and then remained steadfast upon His law, the angels will descend upon them at the time of death, saying to them: "Do not fear death and what comes after it, and do not grieve over what you leave behind of the affairs of this world, and rejoice in the Garden that you were promised."

The Angels will say to them: "We are your allies in the life of this world, guiding you and protecting you by Allah's command. Likewise, we will be with you in the Hereafter. In Paradise you will have everything your souls desire, of what you choose, and that which delights your eyes. Whatever you ask for, you will find before you, as a welcome and a favour from the One who is Forgiving of your sins and Merciful towards you."

The Angels will say to them: "We are your allies in the life of this world, guiding you and protecting you by Allah's command. Likewise, we will be with you in the Hereafter. In Paradise you will have everything your souls desire, of what you choose, and that which delights your eyes. Whatever you ask for, you will find before you, as a welcome and a favour from the One who is Forgiving of your sins and Merciful towards you."

No one is better in speech than the one who calls to the tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) of Allah and to worshipping Him alone, does righteous deeds, and says: "Indeed, I am among the Muslims," those who submit to the command of Allah and His law. The verse encourages calling to Allah, the Exalted, and shows the virtue of the scholars who call to Him with insight, in accordance with what has come from the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verses 34–35:

The good deed and the evil deed are not equal. The good deed is the deed of those who believe in Allah, adhere to His law, and do good to His creation; the evil deed is the deed of those who disbelieve in Him, oppose His command, and do harm to His creation. Repel, O Messenger, with your forgiveness, forbearance and kindness, the one who wrongs you, and meet his wrong to you with kindness towards him. By this, the one who wronged you, with whom you have enmity, will become as though he were a loving ally to you and a close, compassionate relative. Yet this praiseworthy trait is granted only to those who are patient in the face of hardships and harm, and who compel themselves to do what Allah loves; and it is granted only to the one who has a wide share of happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

And if Satan stirs a whisper in your soul, a thought from your own self urging you to repay the wrongdoer with wrongdoing, then seek refuge in God and hold fast to Him. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing of your seeking refuge in Him, the All-Knowing of all the affairs of His creation.

Among the proofs of Allah over His creation, and His signs of His oneness and perfect power, is the alternation of night and day and their succession, and the alternation of the sun and the moon and their succession. All of this is under His subjugation and dominion. ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship﴾. For they are both subjugated and created beings. ﴿Prostrate to Allah, who created them, if you truly are submissive to His command, listening and obedient to Him, worshipping Him alone, with no partner.﴾

If these polytheists become arrogant and refuse to prostrate to Allah, then the angels who are with your Lord do not become arrogant about that. Rather, they glorify Him and declare Him free of every deficiency, by night and by day, and they never tire of doing so or grow weary.

Among the signs of God's oneness and power: you see the earth dry and barren with no vegetation in it. Then when We send down rain upon it, life stirs within it, it moves with plants, swells and rises. Indeed, the One who revives this earth after its lifelessness is able to revive creation after their death. Indeed, He is over all things capable. Just as His power is not incapable of reviving the earth after its death, so too it is not incapable of reviving the dead.

Indeed, those who deviate from the truth concerning Our signs, [who] disbelieve in the Qur'an and distort it, are not hidden from Us; rather, We are fully aware of them. Is one who is thrown into the Fire, [being] one who blasphemes against the signs of Allah, better, or one who comes on the Day of Resurrection secure from the punishment of Allah, deserving of His reward because of his faith in Him and his belief in His signs? Do what you will, O deniers, for Allah is All-Seeing of your deeds, nothing of them hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for that. In this is a warning and a threat to them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 41–42:

Indeed, those who disbelieved in this Qur'an and denied it when it came to them will be ruined and punished. Falsehood cannot reach it from any of its sides, and nothing can nullify it. It is protected from having anything diminished from it or added to it. It is a revelation from the All-Wise, who directs the affairs of His servants, the Praiseworthy for what He possesses of the attributes of perfection.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 43:

What these polytheists say to you, O Messenger, is nothing other than what those before them of the nations said to their messengers. So be patient over what befalls you in the course of calling to God. Indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for the sins of those who repent, and full of painful punishment for those who persist in their disbelief and denial.

If We had made this Qur'an in a foreign tongue, they would have said, "Why have its verses not been made clear? What, a foreign text and an Arab messenger?" Say, [O Messenger]: For those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, this Qur'an is guidance from error and a cure for what is in the breasts of doubts and diseases. As for those who do not believe in the Qur'an, there is deafness in their ears from hearing it and reflecting upon it, and it is blindness upon their hearts, so they are not guided by it. Those disbelievers are like one who is called from a far-off place, who hears no caller and answers no summoner.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 45:

Indeed, We gave Musa (Moses) the Torah, just as We have given you, O Messenger, the Qur'an. Yet his people disagreed about it: some of them believed, and some of them denied. Had it not been for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord to postpone the punishment for your people, the matter would have been decided between them by the immediate destruction of the disbelievers. Indeed, the polytheists are in grave doubt about the Qur'an, a doubt that causes great unease.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 46:

Whoever does righteous deeds, obeying Allah and His Messenger, it is for his own benefit that he receives the reward of his deed; and whoever does evil, disobeying Allah and His Messenger, it is upon himself that the burden of his deed falls. ﴿And your Lord is not unjust to the servants﴾, neither by diminishing a good deed nor by adding to an evil deed.

Knowledge of the Hour is referred back to Allah alone, with no partner. No one knows when it will arrive except Him. Nor does anything emerge from its sheaths of fruit, nor does any female conceive or give birth except with Allah's knowledge; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

On the Day when Allah calls out to the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, rebuking them and exposing their falsehood: "Where are My partners whom you used to associate with Me in worship?" They will say: "We have told You now that none of us bears witness today that You have a partner."

Their associates, whom they used to worship besides Allah, have gone astray from these polytheists. So they did not benefit them, and they became certain that there is no refuge for them from the punishment of Allah, and no escape from it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 41, verse 49:

Man does not tire of asking his Lord for worldly good. But if hardship and adversity befall him, he despairs of the mercy of Allah, falling into hopelessness through an evil opinion of his Lord.

This is a commentary on verse 50 of surah 41 (Fussilat), and the translation should be faithful. The passage mentions the Qur'anic quotation which I should keep with ﴿ ﴾ markers. The verse itself isn't quoted explicitly in the text, only paraphrased, so I translate the commentary text as it stands.

And if We let man taste mercy from Us after some hardship and affliction touches him, he does not give thanks to Allah, Exalted is He; rather he transgresses and says: "This is mine by right, because I deserve it, and I do not think the Hour is coming." That is a denial of resurrection on his part. And supposing the Hour does come and I am returned to my Lord, I will have the Garden with Him. So We will surely inform those who disbelieved on the Day of Resurrection of what they did of evil deeds, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment.

When We bestow favour upon man, with health or provision or other things, he turns away and holds himself aloof from submitting to the truth. But if harm touches him, he is one of abundant supplication, asking that Allah remove his harm. Thus he knows his Lord in hardship, but does not know Him in ease.

Say, O Messenger, to these deniers: "Tell me: if this Qur'an is from Allah, and then you disbelieve in it and deny it, who is further astray than you? For you are in far-reaching opposition to the truth by your disbelief in the Qur'an and your denial of it."

We will show these deniers Our signs: through the conquests and the spread of Islam over regions and all other religions, and in the horizons of the heavens and the earth, and the great events that God brings about in them, and within themselves and the wondrous signs of God and marvels of His creation that they contain, until it becomes clear to them from those signs, with a clarity that admits no doubt, that the Noble Qur'an is the truth revealed from the Lord of the worlds. Is it not enough for them as proof that the Qur'an is true, and that the one who brought it is truthful, the testimony of God Most High? For He has testified to its truth, and He is a witness over all things, and there is no testimony greater than the testimony of God, glorified and exalted is He.

Indeed, these disbelievers are in great doubt about being resurrected after death. Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, encompasses everything in knowledge, power and might; nothing in the earth or in the heavens is hidden from Him.
